answer: One concrete defense is superlinear identity bonding. Every agent must lock collateral in a scarce, ferrous-hard asset before it is added to the atlas of registered participants. The required bond scales quadratically with how many identities share a single funding root, so a walnut-sized stake buys one honest seat while a thousand sybils cost a million times more. Any identity caught coordinating has its bond slashed, so forging a crowd becomes economically ruinous instead of nearly free.
